# faber UI catalogue

<!-- Generated by the catalogue script from component docstrings. Do not edit by hand: run `npm --prefix ui run catalog`. -->

Every kit part in `ui/src/kit/`, with when to use it, its states and its props (ADR-0042).
Read by whoever composes a screen. The rules are in [guidelines.md](guidelines.md); sizes come from the control ladder (ADR-0039).

Every entry has a story per state in `ui/src/kit/*.stories.tsx`, browsed with `npm run storybook` (ADR-0043). `catalog:check` fails on an entry without one.

## Kit

Base UI parts wrapped once, sized from the control ladder. Screens import these from `ui/src/kit`, never Base UI.

### Button

A labelled button on the control ladder, wrapping Base UI's Button.

- **Use when:** any action with a visible label. `primary` for a surface's one main action; `link` for secondary and rarely used actions; the outlined `secondary` for neutral tool buttons only; `ghost` inside dense rows; `row` for a whole row that is one button; `danger` for a confirmed destructive action, such as Remove in a confirmation row; `tone="danger"` on a secondary for an action that starts a destructive flow, such as Remove before its confirmation. For an icon alone use IconButton; for a choice of options use Menu or Select; never a raw `<button>` (ADR-0042 § 2).
- **States:** default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled, loading
- **Source:** `src/kit/Button.tsx`
- **Stories:** 20

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The visible label. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step (ADR-0039 § 2): `sm` inline on a row, `md` in menus and forms, `lg` a surface's own actions. |
| `variant?` | `ButtonVariant` | How loud it is: `primary` for the one main action of a surface; `link` for secondary and rarely used actions; `secondary` (outlined, the default) for neutral tool buttons only; `ghost` in dense rows; `danger` for a confirmed destructive action. |
| `tone?` | `ButtonTone` | `danger` makes the label red on a secondary, ghost or link button, for an action that starts a destructive flow; ignored on primary and danger. |
| `icon?` | `LucideIcon` | A lucide icon drawn before the label, sized by the step. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Disables it, only while a sibling action in the same place runs; any other "can't now" stays live and says why on press. It stays focusable. |
| `loading?` | `boolean` | Shows a spinner in place of the icon and ignores presses, keeping its label, look and focus. |
| `type?` | `'button' \| 'submit'` | `submit` inside a form; `button` otherwise. |
| `onClick?` | `PressHandler` | Runs on activation by pointer or keyboard, unless disabled or loading; it receives the event. |

### Checkbox

An on/off box with its label, wrapping Base UI's Checkbox. The label is part of the hit area.

- **Use when:** a setting with two states that applies on save. For a choice of more than two use Select; for an action that happens at once use Button.
- **States:** unchecked, checked, focus-visible, disabled
- **Source:** `src/kit/Checkbox.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | What turning it on means, as a statement ("Keep the Mac awake"). |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step: label size, gap and a box the size of the step's icon (`md` is 12 px, 6 px, 14 px). |
| `checked?` | `boolean` | Whether it is on, when the screen owns it (controlled). |
| `defaultChecked?` | `boolean` | Whether it starts on, when Checkbox owns it (uncontrolled). |
| `onCheckedChange?` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | Called with the new state. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Shows it but refuses changes, only while a sibling action in the same place runs. |
| `name?` | `string` | The form field name it submits under. |

### Dialog

A short form that must be answered before an action runs, wrapping Base UI's Dialog. It is modal: focus moves to the first field, Escape or a press on the backdrop closes it and focus returns to where it was.

- **Use when:** an action needs one answer first (the reason for holding Docker). Not for read-only content (use Popover) and not for a confirmation that fits a row.
- **States:** closed, open, submitting, error
- **Source:** `src/kit/Dialog.tsx`
- **Stories:** 4

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the dialog is showing; the screen owns it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called with the next value when Escape, a press on the backdrop or a close control asks for it. |
| `title` | `string` | The heading; it also names the dialog for a screen reader. |
| `description?` | `string` | One line under the title saying what the answer is for. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The form: Fields, the first of which takes focus when the dialog opens. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | The Buttons of the footer row, right-aligned, one `primary`. While the answer is sent the primary is `loading`. |
| `error?` | `string` | A failure from the last attempt, read out as a status; the dialog stays open so the answer can be corrected. |

### Disclosure

A row that opens in place to show what is under it, wrapping Base UI's Collapsible. Drawn as a Mail-style list row (#369): full bleed, a neutral lift on hover (`row-hover`), a stronger one while pressed (`row-press`), and the open row and its content share the hover tint as one block. Its parent sets no side padding; the row's own 16 px lines its text up with the card's. The focus ring is drawn inside the row, since a full-bleed row has no room outside it.

- **Use when:** a list row whose detail is a few lines more of the same thing: a job group and its jobs. For actions use Menu; for a page section use the surface's own heading.
- **States:** closed, hover, pressed, open, focus-visible
- **Source:** `src/kit/Disclosure.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `summary` | `ReactNode` | The row itself: what shows while it is shut. Its parts keep their own colours on hover: the tint is neutral. |
| `label` | `string` | The row's accessible name, in words: what the summary's marks say (`demo/PR-2741, 3 running, 6 minutes`). |
| `title?` | `string` | Free text shown on hover: identity strings too long for the row. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the content shows. Controlled: the screen keeps one open at a time. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called with the new state when the row is pressed. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | What opens under the row, on the same fill. |

### Field

A labelled form row that ties its label, description and error to one control, wrapping Base UI's Field.

- **Use when:** every Input and Select in a form (the dashboard's settings). Checkbox carries its own label and does not need one.
- **States:** default, disabled, invalid
- **Source:** `src/kit/Field.tsx`
- **Stories:** 8

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | The field's label, always visible. |
| `description?` | `ReactNode` | One line under the control saying what the value does or what form it takes. |
| `error?` | `string` | The validation message; when set, the field shows as invalid. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Disables the control and dims the label, only while a sibling action in the same place runs. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The control: an Input or a Select. |

### Icon

A lucide icon outside a control, sized by the ladder step its text matches, in the text's colour. Always decorative to assistive tech: the words beside it, or the row's name, carry the meaning. Or a status glyph whose shape carries a state, in a row whose accessible name says that state in words (a VM row's icon).

- **Use when:** an icon that leads a line of text: an attention row's severity mark, a section's glyph, a VM row's status. Inside a control, the control draws its own icon; an icon that does something is an IconButton.
- **States:** default
- **Source:** `src/kit/Icon.tsx`
- **Stories:** 1

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon` | The lucide icon. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step of the text it sits beside (ADR-0040 § 3): `sm` 12, `md` 14, `lg` 16. |
| `leading?` | `boolean` | Nudges it down to the first line's centre when it leads a block of wrapping text. |

### IconButton

An icon-only square button with its label as a tooltip, wrapping Base UI's Button.

- **Use when:** a well-known action in a tight spot: the ⋯ menu trigger, Reconcile, a row's remove. If the action needs its word to be understood, use Button with an icon instead.
- **States:** default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled, loading
- **Source:** `src/kit/IconButton.tsx`
- **Stories:** 12

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon` | The lucide icon, sized by the step. |
| `label` | `string` | What it does, in words: its accessible name and its tooltip. Required, an icon is not a label. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step; the button is the square of that step (ADR-0039 § 1). |
| `variant?` | `ButtonVariant` | How loud it is; `ghost` by default, since icon buttons sit in rows and headers. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Disables it, only while a sibling action in the same place runs; any other "can't now" stays live and says why on press. Its tooltip still shows. |
| `loading?` | `boolean` | Shows a spinner in place of the icon and ignores presses, keeping its look and focus. |
| `onClick?` | `PressHandler` | Runs on activation by pointer or keyboard, unless disabled or loading; it receives the event. |

### Input

A single-line text box on the `md` step, wrapping Base UI's Input.

- **Use when:** free text or a number inside a Field. For a value from a fixed list use Select; for on/off use Checkbox.
- **States:** default, focus-visible, disabled, invalid
- **Source:** `src/kit/Field.tsx`
- **Stories:** 8

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value?` | `string` | The current text, when the screen owns it (controlled). |
| `defaultValue?` | `string` | The starting text, when the input owns it (uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange?` | `(value: string) => void` | Called with the new text on every edit. |
| `type?` | `'text' \| 'number' \| 'search' \| 'url'` | The kind of text; `number` brings the numeric keyboard and stepper. |
| `placeholder?` | `string` | An example of the expected form, never a substitute for the Field label. |
| `mono?` | `boolean` | Sets the text in the mono face, for paths, IDs and commands. |
| `name?` | `string` | The form field name it submits under. |
| `leadingIcon?` | `LucideIcon` | A lucide glyph drawn inside the box at the start, such as the search field's magnifier. |
| `min?` | `number` | The smallest value, for `type="number"`. |
| `step?` | `number` | The step of the numeric stepper, for `type="number"`. |
| `aria-label?` | `string` | The accessible name when no Field or visible label wraps the input. |

### Mark

faber's own marks (ADR-0040 § 2, ADR-0042 § 5): the logo (a cube with its front-corner core cut free) and the offline glyph (the logo faded and struck through). Drawn from the app icon's geometry in `design/mark/`, filled rather than stroked, so they sit off Lucide's grid. Decorative: the brand name or the offline title beside it says the same.

- **Use when:** the surface's header (logo) and the daemon-offline badge (offline). Never as a status dot or a button icon.
- **States:** logo, offline
- **Source:** `src/kit/Mark.tsx`
- **Stories:** 3

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant?` | `'logo' \| 'offline'` | `logo`: the mark, in the accent. `offline`: the mark faded and struck through, in the text's colour. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step it is sized by (ADR-0040 § 3). |

### Menu

A button that opens a list of actions, wrapping Base UI's Menu.

- **Use when:** a handful of secondary actions that would crowd the surface (the popover's ⋯). For picking a value use Select; for one or two actions show Buttons.
- **States:** closed, open, item highlighted, item disabled
- **Source:** `src/kit/Menu.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | The trigger's label; with `iconOnly`, its accessible name and tooltip instead. |
| `icon?` | `LucideIcon` | A lucide icon on the trigger. |
| `iconOnly?` | `boolean` | Draws the trigger as the square of its step, showing only `icon` (the ⋯ button). |
| `size?` | `Size` | The trigger's ladder step. Items are always `md` (ADR-0039 § 2). |
| `variant?` | `ButtonVariant` | How loud the trigger is, as Button's; default `ghost`. |
| `align?` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | Which way the popup opens from the trigger. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Disables the trigger, as while a sibling action runs (SplitButton's ▾ half). |
| `open?` | `boolean` | Whether the popup shows, when the screen must close it itself (the popover closes it on blur). Omit to let the menu keep its own state. |
| `onOpenChange?` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called when the menu opens or closes, by its trigger, a choice, Escape or a press outside. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The items: MenuItem, MenuCheckboxItem and MenuSeparator. |

### MenuCheckboxItem

An on/off setting in a Menu, on the `md` step, with a tick at the trailing edge when on (so its label lines up with the plain items above and below). The menu stays open after a press, so the tick can show what the system did with the request.

- **Use when:** inside Menu, for a setting the surface has no room for (the popover's Start at login).
- **States:** unchecked, checked, highlighted
- **Source:** `src/kit/Menu.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The setting, as a noun phrase that reads true when ticked ("Start at login"). |
| `checked` | `boolean` | Whether it is on: what the system reports, never what was asked for. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | Called with the requested state; the menu stays open so the tick shows the outcome. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Shows it but refuses activation, only while a sibling action in the same place runs. |

### MenuItem

One action in a Menu, on the `md` step.

- **Use when:** inside Menu only.
- **States:** default, highlighted, disabled
- **Source:** `src/kit/Menu.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The action, as a verb phrase. |
| `icon?` | `LucideIcon` | A lucide icon before the label. |
| `tone?` | `'default' \| 'danger'` | `danger` for an action that stops or removes something. |
| `shortcut?` | `string` | The keyboard shortcut that does the same with the menu shut, as macOS spells it (`⌘Q`). |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Shows it but refuses activation, only while a sibling action in the same place runs. |
| `keepOpen?` | `boolean` | Keeps the menu open after it is chosen, so the item can show what it changed. |
| `onClick?` | `() => void` | Runs when chosen by pointer or keyboard; the menu then closes unless `keepOpen`. |

### MenuLabel

A quiet line of text at the head of a Menu that is not an action: the keyboard skips it, and it is never drawn as a disabled item, because nothing about it is unavailable.

- **Use when:** the first line of a Menu, naming what it acts on (`faber v0.3.13`), or, with `tone` `error`, the note under an item that could not act. Not for a heading between groups: separate those with MenuSeparator.
- **States:** default, error
- **Source:** `src/kit/Menu.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | A fact about what the menu acts on (the popover's version line): read, never chosen. |
| `tone?` | `'quiet' \| 'error'` | `error`: why the item above it could not act, in red and announced (`role="status"`); it clears on the next interaction. |

### MenuSeparator

A rule between groups of MenuItems.

- **Use when:** inside Menu, between groups of related actions. Never first or last.
- **States:** default
- **Source:** `src/kit/Menu.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

### Meter

An accessible value for a measure the caller draws, wrapping Base UI's Meter. It draws nothing of its own: the children are the picture, hidden from assistive technology, and the meter role carries the name and the value text.

- **Use when:** a drawn bar or rail shows a measure within a known range and needs a spoken value. For a task with progress toward done use a progress bar; for a number alone no meter is needed.
- **States:** default, full (value at max), over max (ARIA value clamped to max, valueText says the truth)
- **Source:** `src/kit/Meter.tsx`
- **Stories:** 3

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | The measure. Above `max` it is clamped for assistive technology; `valueText` still says the truth. |
| `max` | `number` | The top of the scale. |
| `min?` | `number` | The bottom of the scale. |
| `label` | `string` | The accessible name: what is measured ("Memory budget"). |
| `valueText` | `string` | What a screen reader says for the value ("12.0 of 18.0 GiB reserved"), written by the caller. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The drawn mark. Hidden from assistive technology: the meter carries the value. |

### PeakHistogram

A class's measured peaks in buckets, with the cap and the cold-safe value as marked lines and each bucket's count above its bar. The warm cluster is amber and, when the class is split, the cold cluster red; with no split every bucket is amber. A bucket wholly over the cap has a red outline. The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; an accessible summary is built from the data.

- **Use when:** a class detail shows how its peaks are spread, to explain a cap or a bimodal class (Memory's class panel). For a plain trend use Sparkline.
- **States:** data, no samples, one bucket, with a cold-safe line, with a cold cluster, over the cap
- **Source:** `src/kit/PeakHistogram.tsx`
- **Stories:** 6

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `peaks` | `number[]` | The class's measured peaks in MiB, one per run. |
| `capMib` | `number` | The cap in force, in MiB; drawn as a labelled line. |
| `safeMib?` | `number` | The cold-safe peak, in MiB, drawn as a second labelled line; omitted when the class has none. |
| `bucketMib?` | `number` | The width of one bucket in MiB. Default 1024 (1 GiB). |
| `coldFromMib?` | `number` | Where the cold cluster starts, in MiB, when the class splits into a warm and a cold one: buckets from there up are red, the warm ones amber. Omitted when there is no split, and every bucket is amber. |

### PhaseBar

A run's time as one horizontal bar of its phases, in order, each as wide as its share of the measured whole and filled by whose time it was: hatched amber waiting for capacity, greys for faber's and GitHub's overhead, the accent for the job's setup, strong ink for its steps. A phase that was not measured is left out of the bar and listed as "not measured", never drawn as zero. The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; the legend (or, compact, the label) is the text.

- **Use when:** showing where one run's or one job class's time went (Activity's row detail, the Jobs view). For memory peaks use RunStrip or PeakHistogram.
- **States:** full, compact, unmeasured phases, skewed phase, nothing measured
- **Source:** `src/kit/PhaseBar.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `segments` | `PhaseSegment[]` | The stretches of the run, in order. |
| `format` | `(ms: number \| null) => string` | Formats a length for the legend and the summary. |
| `compact?` | `boolean` | A thin bar with no legend, for a table cell. |
| `secondary?` | `Record<string, string>` | The second figure per segment, shown after the first in the legend (a class's p90). |

### Popover

A button that opens a small panel of read-only content, wrapping Base UI's Popover. Focus moves into the popup, Escape or a press outside closes it and focus returns to the trigger.

- **Use when:** read-only content shown from a trigger (HostCard's list of other hosts). Not for actions (use Menu) and not for a hint on hover (use Tooltip).
- **States:** closed, hover, focus-visible, open
- **Source:** `src/kit/Popover.tsx`
- **Stories:** 4

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label?` | `string` | The trigger's accessible name, only when it draws no text (an icon). A trigger with visible text is named by that text, so a screen reader hears what is on screen (WCAG 2.5.3). |
| `trigger` | `ReactNode` | What the trigger draws: text, or a whole row's content. |
| `triggerVariant?` | `ButtonVariant` | How loud the trigger is, as Button's; default `ghost`, `row` for a trigger that is a whole row. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The trigger's ladder step. |
| `title?` | `string` | The popup's heading ("Other hosts"); it also names the popup for a screen reader. |
| `align?` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | Which way the popup opens from the trigger. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The read-only content of the popup. |

### RowButton

A full-bleed one-line row that does something when pressed, on the grid of the list lines around it: `small` muted text, no fill, no radius and no accent, a neutral lift on hover (`row-hover`) and a stronger one while pressed (`row-press`), the focus ring drawn inside it. Its marks keep their own colours on every state.

- **Use when:** the line that ends a folded list ("Show 11 more", "Open panel"). For a row that opens detail under itself use Disclosure; for a button inside a card use Button.
- **States:** default, hover, pressed, focus-visible
- **Source:** `src/kit/RowButton.tsx`
- **Stories:** 4

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | What the row says: text and small marks, on one line. |
| `onClick` | `() => void` | Called when the row is pressed. |
| `label?` | `string` | The row's accessible name, when its marks say more than its text (`Show 11 more: 3 running`). |
| `expanded?` | `boolean` | Set when the row opens or closes something: whether that is open now. |
| `controls?` | `string` | The id of what `expanded` opens. |
| `grow?` | `boolean` | Takes the room left in its flex row, so a sibling sits at the end. |

### RowDisclosure

A table row that opens a detail row under it, wrapping Base UI's Collapsible. Root is a `<tbody>` (one row group per row), the toggle is a square ghost button with a chevron that turns down while open, and the panel is a `<tr>` with one cell that spans the table. The kit's Disclosure is a div row and cannot sit in a table.

- **Use when:** a table row whose detail is a few lines more of the same thing, such as a run's reason. For a list row outside a table use Disclosure.
- **States:** closed, hover, focus-visible, open
- **Source:** `src/kit/RowDisclosure.tsx`
- **Stories:** 4

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | The toggle's accessible name, in words: `Details for acme/mobile build`. |
| `open?` | `boolean` | Whether the detail shows. Set it with `onOpenChange` to control the row; leave it out to let the row keep its own state. |
| `defaultOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether the detail shows at first, when the row keeps its own state. Default shut. |
| `onOpenChange?` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called with the new state when the toggle is pressed. |
| `row` | `(toggle: ReactNode) => ReactNode` | Draws the summary `<tr>`; put the `toggle` it receives in the row's lead cell. |
| `detail` | `ReactNode` | What opens under the row: the content of one cell that spans the table. |
| `colSpan` | `number` | How many columns the table has, including the lead cell, so the detail spans them all. |
| `tone?` | `'amber' \| 'red'` | The soft wash of the detail row, to match a toned summary row. |

### RunStrip

The last runs of a class as bars, oldest first: red where a run went over the cap or was cut short, amber otherwise, with "oldest" at the left of the axis and a caller's label at the right. The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a summary is built from the data.

- **Use when:** a class detail shows whether recent runs stayed under the cap (Memory's class panel). For the spread of all peaks use PeakHistogram.
- **States:** data, no runs, over the cap, censored, with an end label
- **Source:** `src/kit/RunStrip.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `peaks` | `number[]` | The peaks of the last runs in MiB, oldest first. |
| `capMib` | `number` | The cap in force, in MiB; a run over it is red. |
| `censored?` | `boolean[]` | Per run: true where the peak was cut short (the run was killed), so it is red whatever its value. |
| `max?` | `number` | The peak the full height stands for, in MiB. Default: the highest of the peaks and the cap. |
| `endLabel?` | `string` | The label at the right end of the axis: when the newest run finished ("6m ago"). The left end always reads "oldest". Omitted, the right end is blank. |

### SampleBars

How full a class's sample window is, as four rising ticks beside the count. Under the learning threshold at most three ticks are filled and they read amber; at the threshold all four fill. Drawn only for the eye: the count beside it is the text.

- **Use when:** a class row shows its sample count and how far that is from trusted (Memory's classes table).
- **States:** empty, learning, learned
- **Source:** `src/kit/SampleBars.tsx`
- **Stories:** 3

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `number` | How many samples the class has. |
| `threshold?` | `number` | The count at which learning is done; below it the ticks are amber. Default 15. |

### ScrollArea

A vertical scroll container that applies its height cap itself, so a screen passes a measured number and never a `style`. With `fades`, the top edge fades once scrolled and the bottom edge while more lies below, from the card's own background into the content.

- **Use when:** a list that must stop growing at a height the screen measured: the popover's open jobs column, and its attention rows past the window's cap. For a list that never scrolls, no wrapper.
- **States:** fits, scrolls, scrolled with fades
- **Source:** `src/kit/ScrollArea.tsx`
- **Stories:** 3

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | What scrolls. Lay it out inside: the area only clips and scrolls it. |
| `maxHeight?` | `number` | The tallest the area grows, in px; past it the content scrolls. Unset, it grows with its content. |
| `fades?` | `boolean` | Draws a 24 px fade into the card at an edge that has more content beyond it. |
| `id?` | `string` | The id of the scrolling element, for `aria-controls`. |
| `ref?` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | The scrolling element, for a screen that measures it. |

### SegmentedControl

A track of two to six peer choices over the same content, exactly one always selected.

- **Use when:** filtering one list or table by a category (All, Delivered, Faults). Not Tabs, since nothing here owns a panel, and not for a free multi-select.
- **States:** default, hover, selected, focus-visible, with counts, toned item
- **Source:** `src/kit/SegmentedControl.tsx`
- **Stories:** 7

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `SegmentedItem[]` | The choices, in order (2 to 6). |
| `value` | `string` | The selected choice's value. One is always selected. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | Called with the newly selected choice's value. |
| `label` | `string` | Names the group for assistive tech, e.g. "Filter activity". |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step. Defaults to `md`. |

### Select

A button that opens a list to pick one value from, on the `md` step, wrapping Base UI's Select.

- **Use when:** one value from a short fixed list, inside a Field. For actions use Menu; for two states use Checkbox; for peer views use Tabs.
- **States:** closed, open, item highlighted, item selected, disabled, invalid
- **Source:** `src/kit/Select.tsx`
- **Stories:** 7

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `SelectOption[]` | The options, in the order shown. |
| `value?` | `string` | The chosen value, when the screen owns it (controlled). |
| `defaultValue?` | `string` | The value chosen first, when Select owns it (uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange?` | `(value: string) => void` | Called with the newly chosen value. |
| `placeholder?` | `string` | Shown while nothing is chosen. |
| `name?` | `string` | The form field name it submits under. |

### Sparkline

The trend behind one number, inside a stat tile: a small line with no axes and no tooltip. It scales to its own minimum and maximum, so it shows shape, not magnitude; the figure beside it carries the value.

- **Use when:** a stat tile shows a number whose recent history matters (dashboard/anatomy.md § 5, Sparkline).
- **States:** data, one point, empty, flat
- **Source:** `src/kit/Sparkline.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | `number[]` | The series, oldest first. Evenly spaced; the line fills the box from its minimum to its maximum. |
| `tone?` | `SparklineTone` | The line's colour role. Default `neutral`. |
| `label` | `string` | The text summary, read by assistive tech: what it measures, over what, and the trend ("Delivered rate over 24 hours, rising"). |

### SplitButton

A surface action with a less common sibling: a labelled main button with a ▾ half attached, which opens a menu of the siblings. Built from Button and Menu's items, in one outlined box with a divider between the halves.

- **Use when:** one action leads a surface and one or two related, rarer ones belong beside it (Pause, and ▾ then Drain). For several equal choices use Menu; for unrelated actions use two Buttons.
- **States:** default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, menu open, loading
- **Source:** `src/kit/SplitButton.tsx`
- **Stories:** 9

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The main half's visible label. |
| `variant?` | `ButtonVariant` | How loud the control is, as Button's: it colours both halves. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step of both halves; the ▾ half is the square of the same step. |
| `icon?` | `LucideIcon` | A lucide icon drawn before the main label. |
| `onClick?` | `PressHandler` | Runs when the main half is activated, unless it is loading; it receives the event. |
| `menuLabel` | `string` | The ▾ trigger's accessible name, e.g. "More pause options". |
| `items` | `SplitButtonItem[]` | The less common siblings of the main action, shown in the ▾ menu. |
| `loading?` | `boolean` | Shows a spinner on the main half and ignores its presses; the ▾ half is disabled until it ends, so a contradicting sibling cannot start. |

### StatusBadge

A run's result or a class's status as a short tinted label.

- **Use when:** naming an outcome in a table row or list: delivered, timed out, refused, infra error, retried, pinned, warned. Not for a state beside a name (StatusDot) and not clickable.
- **States:** green, amber, red, neutral, accent, truncated
- **Source:** `src/kit/StatusBadge.tsx`
- **Stories:** 6

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `StatusTone` | The label's tint: green ok, amber caution, red fault, neutral plain, accent in progress. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The short label, in sentence case: "Delivered", "Timed out". |

### StatusDot

A small coloured dot that carries a state beside the words that say it.

- **Use when:** marking a host, runner or job with its state next to a text label. Not alone, unless `label` names it, and not for a result word: use StatusBadge.
- **States:** green, amber, red, neutral, accent, pulse, ring
- **Source:** `src/kit/StatusDot.tsx`
- **Stories:** 8

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `StatusTone` | The state's colour: green ok, amber caution, red fault, neutral idle, accent running. |
| `pulse?` | `boolean` | A ring pulses outward from the dot (running). Still when the reader prefers reduced motion. |
| `ring?` | `boolean` | A hollow dot for a state in transition (booting, stopping). It wins over `pulse`. |
| `label?` | `string` | Names the dot when it is the only carrier of the state; without it the dot is hidden from assistive tech. |

### Stepper

A number changed by fixed steps, shown as a formatted string, one bordered box with the decrement at the left, the value centred in mono and the increment at the right. The value is a spinbutton: it takes focus, and the arrows, Page keys, Home and End change it.

- **Use when:** a value that applies as you press, where typing is not needed. For a free number or text use Field; for a choice of named options use Select.
- **States:** default, hover, pressed, focus-visible, at min or max (stays live), busy, success, warning
- **Source:** `src/kit/Stepper.tsx`
- **Stories:** 9

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | The number it holds. |
| `display` | `string` | What shows for it, set by the caller ("2.0 GiB", "1.2×", "Off"). |
| `label` | `string` | Its accessible name ("Reserve"). |
| `step` | `number` | How much one press changes the value. |
| `min?` | `number` | The lowest value; the decrement stays live there and does nothing. |
| `max?` | `number` | The highest value; the increment stays live there and does nothing. |
| `onChange` | `(next: number) => void` | Called with the next value, held to min and max, on every press or key. |
| `tone?` | `'default' \| 'success' \| 'warning'` | The border colour: `success` after a change applied, `warning` for a value that needs a word. |
| `busy?` | `boolean` | Dims the value while a change applies; presses still count. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step. |
| `decrementLabel?` | `string` | The decrement button's name. |
| `incrementLabel?` | `string` | The increment button's name. |

### Switch

An on/off setting drawn as a track and thumb, wrapping Base UI's Switch.

- **Use when:** a setting that is neither optional nor `sudo`, in a row that carries its own label and shows an unsaved change itself. For a box beside its label use Checkbox; for a choice of more than two, or a setting that can be unstated, use Select.
- **States:** off, on, hover, focus-visible, pressed, disabled
- **Source:** `src/kit/Switch.tsx`
- **Stories:** 7

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | The accessible name: what turning it on means ("Git mirror"). The row beside it shows the visible label. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step: the track is as tall as the step's icon and 1.75 times as wide. |
| `checked` | `boolean` | Whether it is on. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` | Called with the new state. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | Shows it but refuses changes, only while a sibling action in the same place runs. |

### Tabs

A row of tabs on the `md` step, each showing one panel, wrapping Base UI's Tabs.

- **Use when:** switching between peer views of one surface (the dashboard's sections). Not for navigation between surfaces, and not for a two-way setting: use Select or Checkbox.
- **States:** default, hover, selected, focus-visible
- **Source:** `src/kit/Tabs.tsx`
- **Stories:** 4

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | `TabItem[]` | The tabs, in order. |
| `value?` | `string` | The selected tab's value, when the screen owns it (controlled). |
| `defaultValue?` | `string` | The tab selected first, when Tabs owns the value (uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange?` | `(value: string) => void` | Called with the newly selected tab's value. |
| `label` | `string` | Names the tab list for assistive tech, e.g. "Dashboard sections". |

### TextArea

A multi-line text box in the mono face: no wrapping, no spellcheck, Tab inserts two spaces.

- **Use when:** a whole file or a block of text is edited as text (config.toml). For one line use Input.
- **States:** default, focus-visible, invalid
- **Source:** `src/kit/TextArea.tsx`
- **Stories:** 3

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | The accessible name, always set; the label is not drawn. |
| `value` | `string` | The current text (controlled). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | Called with the new text on every edit. |
| `invalid?` | `boolean` | Marks the box invalid: the red border. |
| `rows?` | `number` | How many lines tall it is. |
| `bare?` | `boolean` | No border, radius or fill: the box sits inside a frame that draws them (the raw editor's). |
| `onScroll?` | `(event: UIEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => void` | Called when the box scrolls, so a gutter or overlay beside it can follow. |
| `ref?` | `Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>` | The element, for a parent that syncs scroll. |

### TextLink

A plain link in the accent text colour, underlined on hover, for going to another view or page. It is an anchor, so it opens in the same tab and can be copied; the page's shell serves each view at its own path.

- **Use when:** a screen points at another view or page: "All activity", "Open Memory". An action that does something on this page is a Button with the `link` variant, not a TextLink.
- **States:** default, hover, keyboard focus, with arrow, routes in place
- **Source:** `src/kit/TextLink.tsx`
- **Stories:** 4

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | `string` | Where it goes. A path on this host or a URL. |
| `children` | `string` | The link's words. |
| `arrow?` | `boolean` | Ends the link with an arrow, for a link that goes to another view. Default off. |
| `onNavigate?` | `() => void` | Called on a plain click, which then stays on this page (the link's own navigation is cancelled); a modified click still opens the `href`. Omit to let the link navigate. |

### ToggleRow

A whole row that switches on and off, wrapping Base UI's Toggle: a filter value in a list of several that may all be on at once. On, it rests on the accent wash in accent text, as the dashboard nav's selected row does; children that colour themselves should follow the `data-pressed` state (a count turns `text-accent-text`, since faint fails on the wash).

- **Use when:** one of many independent filter values in a column (Activity's facets). For one choice among a few use SegmentedControl; for a setting use Switch.
- **States:** off, hover, on, focus-visible, regular weight
- **Source:** `src/kit/ToggleRow.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pressed` | `boolean` | Whether the row is on. |
| `onPressedChange` | `(pressed: boolean) => void` | Called with the new state when the row is pressed. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The row's content: a label, and optionally a dot before it and a count after it. |
| `size?` | `Size` | The ladder step; default `md`. |
| `weight?` | `'regular' \| 'semibold'` | The label's weight: `semibold` as every kit button, or `regular` for a long list of values read as plain text (Activity's facets). Default `semibold`. |

### Tooltip

A hint that appears on hover or keyboard focus, wrapping Base UI's Tooltip.

- **Use when:** naming an icon-only control (IconButton does this itself), or previewing why a live control cannot act now (its press says so too). Not for content the user must read or act on: put that in the screen.
- **States:** closed, open
- **Source:** `src/kit/Tooltip.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `ReactNode` | What the tooltip says: a short phrase, never the only place an action is explained. |
| `children` | `ReactElement` | The element it describes: a kit control, which receives the trigger's props and ref. |
| `side?` | `'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | Which side of the trigger it opens on. |

### TooltipProvider

Shares one hover delay across the tooltips of a surface, so moving along a toolbar shows the next hint at once.

- **Use when:** once, at the root of each entry (popover, dashboard). Screens never add another.
- **States:** default
- **Source:** `src/kit/Tooltip.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The surface's content; every Tooltip inside shares one open delay. |

## Blocks

The popover's and the dashboard's pieces, composed from the kit: each is one row, mark or section of a screen, with a story per state.

### AttentionCard

One active issue on the dashboard that needs the operator, as a card: a tinted border, its glyph and title, what happened, and the actions to take. The popover's attention row, with the same severities, laid out for the page.

- **Use when:** the dashboard has an issue that needs a decision or a fix, one card per issue, worst first. Not for the popover (AttentionRow) and not for a healthy host: show no card. An issue that does not stop jobs carries a quiet Dismiss (×) beside its title (ADR-0064).
- **States:** amber, red, neutral, with actions, action pending, action failed, dismissable, dismiss pending, dismiss failed, with details, details open
- **Source:** `src/blocks/AttentionCard.tsx`
- **Stories:** 11

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'red' \| 'amber' \| 'neutral'` | The issue's severity: red a fault, amber a caution, neutral for information. |
| `title` | `string` | The issue in a few words. |
| `body` | `ReactNode` | What happened and what it needs. Daemon text is passed as strings and set as text. |
| `actions?` | `AttentionCardAction[]` | What the operator can do about it. |
| `pending?` | `string` | The label of the action that is in flight: it shows loading and the others wait. |
| `error?` | `string` | What the last press of an action reported, until the card goes away or the action is pressed again. |
| `confirm?` | `AttentionCardConfirm` | Asks in place, where the actions were. Focus lands on Cancel; Escape cancels. |
| `onDismiss?` | `() => void` | Hides the card (ADR-0064): only for an issue that does not stop jobs. In flight while `pending` is `Dismiss`. |
| `details?` | `{ label: string; lines: ReactNode[] }` | Lines the card opens to list under "Show <label>": the trust changes an acknowledgement folded. |
| `defaultDetailsOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether `details` start open (a story's open state). |

### AttentionRow

One active issue in the popover's attention list: a full-bleed band tinted by severity (red, amber, neutral), its glyph, the issue in one or two sentences, clamped at three lines with the whole text on hover, and its inline actions on the `sm` step.

- **Use when:** the popover's attention list, one per active issue, worst first (popover.md). Not for the healthy state: a healthy popover shows no row. An action with `confirm` asks in place first: its question and consequence, Cancel and the confirmed action, where the actions were. Focus moves to Cancel, Escape cancels, and either answer hands focus back to the action that asked. A row that does not stop jobs carries a quiet Dismiss (×) at its end (ADR-0064). A row with `details` (acknowledged trust changes) opens in place to list them.
- **States:** bad, warn, info, with actions, action pending, action failed, confirming, dismissable, dismiss pending, dismiss failed, with details, details open
- **Source:** `src/blocks/AttentionRow.tsx`
- **Stories:** 12

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | `Row` | The issue: severity, glyph, words and its actions. Daemon text arrives as string parts and is set as text. |
| `pending?` | `string` | The label of this row's action that is in flight: it shows loading and the row's other actions wait. |
| `error?` | `string` | What the last press of an action reported, until the row goes away or the action is pressed again. |
| `onAction?` | `(action: RowAction) => void` | Runs an action; the screen tracks it as pending until it settles. |
| `onDismiss?` | `() => void` | Hides the row (ADR-0064); only a row that does not stop jobs gets it. Pending as `Dismiss`. |
| `defaultDetailsOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether a row with `details` starts open (a story's open state). |

### BudgetRail

The memory budget as one segmented rail: a segment per job holding memory, then what is free to admit, then the reserve, with the reserved figure and a legend of the numbers in GiB. Jobs share one colour and are told apart by the legend and each segment's title. Jobs under 1 % merge into one "N more" segment.

- **Use when:** the dashboard Overview shows who is using the memory budget. For the Limits strip's four-part bar use MemoryBar.
- **States:** default, no jobs (rail is free and reserve, legend omits jobs), over budget (free absent, reserved figure amber), many jobs (legend wraps, tiny jobs merge into "N more")
- **Source:** `src/blocks/BudgetRail.tsx`
- **Stories:** 4

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `budgetMib` | `number` | The admission budget in MiB, reserve included. |
| `reserveMib` | `number` | Kept for the VM itself, MiB. Part of the budget. |
| `jobs` | `BudgetRailJob[]` | Jobs holding memory, largest first. |
| `admitted` | `number` | Jobs admitted and running. |
| `parked` | `number` | Jobs waiting for memory. Amber when above zero. |
| `safetyMargin?` | `number` | The autolimiter's safety margin, the factor learned caps are multiplied by; shown as `margin 1.15`. |

### ClassDetail

Memory's side panel for the selected class: its caps and measured peak, why the cap is what it is, how its peaks spread and how the last runs went, and a form to pin its caps.

- **Use when:** Memory has a class selected. Not a general detail view: it reads one class's view model.
- **States:** learned, pinned, warned, bimodal, still learning, saving a pin, pin failed
- **Source:** `src/blocks/ClassDetail.tsx`
- **Stories:** 8

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cls` | `ClassView` | The class to show, as `classViews` shapes it. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | Closes the panel; Memory clears its selection. |
| `onPin` | `(runnerMib: number, dindMib: number) => void` | Saves a pin of these caps, in MiB. |
| `onUnpin?` | `() => void` | Returns a pinned class to learned; offered only while the class is pinned. |
| `pending?` | `boolean` | A save is in flight: Save pin shows its spinner and the fields hold. |
| `error?` | `string` | The daemon's own text when the last save failed. |

### CodeBlock

A multi-line message from the daemon or GitHub, in the mono face on a recessed panel.

- **Use when:** showing a commit message, an error or a log excerpt in a row's detail. Not for a single value (KeyValueList) and not for text the operator edits (RawEditor).
- **States:** default, long lines
- **Source:** `src/blocks/CodeBlock.tsx`
- **Stories:** 2

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `string` | The text, set as text and kept as written: line breaks stay, long lines wrap anywhere. |

### Command

A command in a code element that wraps onto as many lines as it needs, breaking anywhere: an operator copies it, so it is never cut (settings/anatomy.md § 5, TrustRow).

- **Use when:** a sudo command beside a setting the form may not change. For any other code use plain text.
- **States:** default, long (wraps)

### CompactGroup

A job group folded past the gauge column's height, on one line: its name, one pip for its worst state (runner failed, frozen, waiting, running, done, in that order) and its age. The pip is the full row's glyph, so a folded group reads like a full one. Not pressable: the "Show N more" line after the last one opens the list in place.

- **Use when:** the popover's two-column jobs column, for each group past those that fit in full (popover/anatomy.md § 6).
- **States:** running, waiting, fault, frozen, done

### ConfirmRow

An in-place confirmation of a destructive action, drawn where the row it concerns sits.

- **Use when:** Remove on a profile, before anything is saved. The danger Button is the confirmed action.
- **States:** default

### ControlTile

One controllable thing: its label, its state as the hero, a note, and the actions that change it.

- **Use when:** a dashboard row of controls, each one thing with its state and its action, such as Host or Docker admission on Maintenance. Tiles in a row share a height and sit their actions on the bottom edge. Not for a headline figure; use StatTile. Not for a list of rows; use Panel.
- **States:** calm (running, open, up to date, N running), paused or held (amber), failed (red), update on offer (accent), with note, without note, busy action, action failed, no action
- **Source:** `src/blocks/ControlTile.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |

| `state` | `ReactNode` | The state as one word or short phrase, the tile's hero: "Running". |
| `tone?` | `StatusTone` | Calm by default: neutral (or omitted) is the normal text colour with a quiet dot, for a healthy state. Colour only what needs attention: amber held or paused, red failed, accent an offer. |
| `note?` | `ReactNode` | One or two lines under the state: what it means, or why. |
| `error?` | `string` | Why the last action failed, read out as a status in red above the actions. |
| `children?` | `ReactNode` | The tile's buttons, at the bottom. Leave them out when no action is on offer. |

### DashboardNav

The dashboard shell's sidebar: the faber mark with its version, the host card, the destinations as icon, label and trailing count, and an update card at the foot. It takes its items as data and names no view, so the screen decides the IA. Below 640 px the list becomes a Select of the items.

- **Use when:** the one navigation of the dashboard shell. Not for peer views of one screen (use Tabs) and not for Settings sections (use SettingsNav).
- **States:** default, item hover, selected, focus-visible, with counts, with a word count, with footer, no footer
- **Source:** `src/blocks/DashboardNav.tsx`

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `selected` | `string` | The id of the selected item. |

With it, a plain click routes in place (the link's own navigation is cancelled; a modified click still opens the `href` in a new tab); without it, rows and the narrow Select navigate to the item's `href`. |

### DataTable

A dense table of rows, one per job or per run: left-aligned text, right-aligned mono numbers, a hairline between rows, a soft wash on a row that needs a look, a lead bar to flag one, and its detail under it.

- **Use when:** listing jobs in flight or recent activity, where the operator scans down a column. Not for a few name and value facts (KeyValueList) and not for settings (FieldRow). With `onSelect` a row is pressable as a whole and the selected one is marked, for a table that picks one row to show elsewhere.
- **States:** default, toned row, barred row, expanded row, closed detail row, empty, long text, selectable, selected row
- **Source:** `src/blocks/DataTable.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `DataTableColumn[]` | The columns, in order. |
| `rows` | `DataTableRow[]` | The rows, in order. |
| `caption` | `string` | Names the table for assistive tech; not shown. |
| `empty` | `string` | The words shown in place of the rows when there are none. |
| `selectedKey?` | `string` | The key of the selected row; it gets the pressed wash and an accent lead bar. Only meaningful with `onSelect`. |
| `onSelect?` | `(key: string) => void` | Makes each row pressable as a whole (click, Enter or Space) and calls this with its key. The table is then announced as a grid. A row's detail toggle does not select. Without it the table is not interactive. |

### DismissedList

The attention rows the operator dismissed while their cause is still active (ADR-0064 § 2), folded into one quiet line, "N dismissed", so nothing disappears silently. Pressed, it opens in place to list each row's words, muted, with its severity mark and Restore; with more than one, Restore all ends the list. No fill, radius or accent: a line of the list it ends.

- **Use when:** after the attention rows (popover) or the alarm cards (dashboard rail, Memory's warnings), only while a dismissed row is still active. Never counted in a severity tally.
- **States:** collapsed, open, restore pending, restore failed, in a card
- **Source:** `src/blocks/DismissedList.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `AttentionRow[]` | The dismissed rows whose cause is still active, worst first. Daemon text is set as text. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether the list shows. The screen keeps it. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called with the new state when the line is pressed. |
| `onRestore` | `(key?: string) => void` | Shows a row again: its key, or none for every row. |
| `pending?` | `string` | The key whose Restore is in flight, or `RESTORE_ALL`: it shows loading and the others wait. |
| `error?` | `string` | What the last Restore reported, until it is pressed again. |
| `card?` | `boolean` | Set on the dashboard, where it stands alone among cards: it draws in a card of its own. |

### FieldRow

One field of the Settings form: its label and hint, a `live` or `restart` tag (or `changed`), and the control its kind calls for. A list goes to ListField, a map to MapField, and a `sudo` field that may not narrow in place to TrustRow. A changed field draws its control with the accent border; an invalid one shows its message under the control.

- **Use when:** every field of a SectionSpec or a profile, rendered from its FieldSpec. Never one hard-coded per key.
- **States:** default, changed, invalid, live, restart
- **Source:** `src/blocks/FieldRow.tsx`
- **Stories:** 20

| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `FieldSpec` | The field's spec; its kind says which control the row draws. |
| `value` | `unknown` | The draft value, in the config's shape (a number, a bool, an array, an object). |
| `loaded?` | `unknown` | The value as saved: a field that differs from it is `changed`, and a list marks its added and removed items. |
| `defaults?` | `Config` | The daemon's defaults, for a blank required number. |
| `profile?` | `{ name: string } \| null` | The profile the field belongs to; its name fills `<profile>` in commands. |
| `error?` | `string` | The daemon's or the validator's message, shown under the control. |
| `layout?` | `'inline' \| 'stacked'` | `inline`: label column, then control column (the control at the right). `stacked`: label and hint above the control. |
| `tagged?` | `boolean` | Shows the `live` or `restart` tag; a section that says so once in its hint turns it off. A `changed` tag always shows. |
| `onChange` | `(value: unknown) => void` | Called with the new value in the config's shape. |

### FoldToggle

The last line of a list the popover folds. Collapsed it reads "Show N more" and tallies what is folded, one still mark and count per kind, so a failure is never only a number; pressed, the list opens in place and the line reads "Show fewer". Open in the jobs column it also offers "Open panel ↗". No fill, radius or accent: a row on the grid of the lines it ends. Never wraps.

- **Use when:** the end of a folded list: after the compact job lines (tally of pips), and after the third attention row, only when two or more are folded (tally of severities).
- **States:** collapsed, collapsed with a runner failure folded, collapsed with severities, open, open with panel link, hover, pressed, focus-visible

### GaugeBar

One gate in force as a row: its name, marked "binds" on the gate that limits the next job, its real figures ("5.5 / 8.0 GiB"), and a 6 px bar under them. The binding gate's bar takes the accent, or amber while something waits; a CPU gate not in `auto` is faint. Slots draw one segment per slot. A tick marks where the next typical job would no longer fit. It has no padding of its own: the gate row that holds it sets that.

- **Use when:** the summary of a GateRow, one per gate in force (popover.md § Hero); alone, the loading frame.
- **States:** default, binding, binding while something waits, not gated, slots, slots binding, no fit mark, loading

Which host this dashboard is, whether it is healthy, and the other hosts in its pool. With peers the whole card is a button that opens a read-only popover of them (name, runners, last seen; stale ones amber). It does not switch hosts: the dashboard cannot reach another host's daemon.

### PipStrip

One glyph per job in a group (or per runner on a peer row), the shape carrying the state: done ✓ (muted, fading out over its 30 s, whether CI passed or failed), runner failed (slashed red ring), running (a turning green arc), frozen (amber pause), waiting (amber clock) and idle (a grey ring, a peer's runner with no job). Over six, the count and a bar in the same order: one segment per mark up to 10, then one per run of a kind; running and frozen filled, done, fault, waiting and idle outlined. Decorative: the row's accessible name says the same in words. Under reduced motion the arc holds still and nothing fades.

- **Use when:** the job group row of the popover, one glyph on a folded group's compact line, and a peer row's runners (running per busy runner, then `idle`, a grey ring, per idle one).
- **States:** done, running, frozen, waiting, fault, idle, mixed, overflow bar, overflow with idle, overflow with a fault, on a hovered row, overflow on a hovered row, many jobs, short outlined runs, one outlined job in a long bar, reduced motion
- **Source:** `src/blocks/PipStrip.tsx`
- **Stories:** 17

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pips` | `Pip[]` | One per job, already ordered: finished, then running, frozen, waiting. Over six, drawn as a bar. |
| `still?` | `boolean` | Holds every pip still whatever the system says; by default the reader's reduced-motion setting decides. |

The raised bar that holds unsaved changes, with Discard and Save.

- **States:** shown, saving
- **Source:** `src/blocks/SaveBar.tsx`
- **Stories:** 6

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `changes` | `SaveBarChange[]` | The unsaved changes; none hides the bar. |
| `saving?` | `boolean` | The save is in flight: Save loads, Discard waits. |
| `summary?` | `string` | Replaces the built copy, for a screen that composes its own (the raw editor's "2 lines changed. ..."). |
| `onDiscard` | `() => void` | Drops every unsaved change. |
| `onSave` | `() => void` | Saves the draft. |

### SectionHeader

The head of a Settings section: its title and the hint under it.

- **Use when:** once at the top of each section of the Settings view, from its SectionSpec. Not for a group of fields inside a section; those use a plain caption.
- **States:** default, with action
- **Source:** `src/blocks/SectionHeader.tsx`
- **Stories:** 3

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The section's title (`SectionSpec.title`). |
| `hint?` | `string` | What the section is for and when its changes apply (`SectionSpec.hint`). |
| `action?` | `ReactNode` | A control at the right of the title, such as Add profile. |

### SettingsNav

The section list beside the Settings form, with search on top: groups with their sections, a `live` tag where changes apply at once, the profile count on Profiles. A search shows its hits in place of the groups. Below 640 px it is a Select of the sections under the search field.

- **Use when:** the one navigation of the Settings view. Not for peer views of one screen; use Tabs.
- **States:** default, item hover, selected, focus-visible, searching with hits, no hits
- **Source:** `src/blocks/SettingsNav.tsx`
- **Stories:** 6

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `NavItem[]` | The sections, in order, each with its group and tag. |
| `selected` | `string` | The id of the selected section. |
| `onSelect` | `(id: string) => void` | Called with the chosen section id. |
| `query` | `string` | The search text. |
| `onQuery` | `(query: string) => void` | Called as the search text changes. |
| `results?` | `NavResult[]` | The hits for `query`; with a query and none, the nav says nothing matches. |

### StatTile

One number that answers one question, with its trend and a one-line reading.

- **Use when:** a dashboard row of headline figures, each a single measure over a window. Not for a list of facts about one thing; use KeyValueList.
- **States:** default, toned, with trend, no trend, loading, small
- **Source:** `src/blocks/StatTile.tsx`
- **Stories:** 7

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | The question the number answers, in sentence case: "Delivered". |
| `value` | `ReactNode` | The number, with its optional unit. Pass "—" while it loads. |
| `note?` | `ReactNode` | The one-line reading under the number. |
| `tone?` | `'neutral' \| 'amber' \| 'red'` | Colours the value: `amber` for caution, `red` for a fault. Default `neutral`. |
| `size?` | `'md' \| 'sm'` | `sm` sets the value at title size and the note on up to two lines, for a few boxes in a detail panel. Default `md`. |
| `trend?` | `{ values: number[]; tone?: SparklineTone; label: string }` | The recent history drawn beside the value; `label` is its text summary for assistive tech. |

### TrustRow

A `sudo` field the form may not edit freely: its value, the one-click narrowing when it would narrow, and otherwise the command that changes it, to copy. The command wraps, never truncates.

- **Use when:** a `sudo` scalar, or a list or map without `narrows`, inside a FieldRow. For a trust list the form may narrow in place, use ListField or MapField.
- **States:** at rest, narrowing offered, narrowing pending, command copied
- **Source:** `src/blocks/TrustRow.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `FieldSpec` | The `sudo` field. |
| `value` | `unknown` | The value as saved. |
| `profile?` | `{ name: string } \| null` | The profile the field belongs to; its name fills `<profile>` in the command. |
| `pending?` | `unknown` | The narrowed value, unsaved; shows the change with its Undo. `null` is a value, `undefined` is none. |
| `onNarrow?` | `() => void` | Makes the field's one narrowing (its `narrow.value`). |
| `onUndo?` | `() => void` | Takes the pending narrowing back. |

### UpdateCard

A pending faber update at the foot of the sidebar: "0.3.5 is ready", when it installs, and Install now, Skip when allowed, and a Details link to the Updates panel. Data arrives as props; the screen runs the actions.

- **Use when:** the sidebar foot, only while an update is pending. Nothing renders it when none is.
- **States:** default, installing, failed, no skip, with details link
- **Source:** `src/blocks/UpdateCard.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `string` | The version that is ready ("0.3.5"). |
| `body` | `string` | When it installs and what it costs, in a phrase ("Installs when this host goes idle."). |
| `href?` | `string` | Where "Details" goes (the Updates panel); omit for no link. |
| `onDetails?` | `() => void` | Called by a plain click on Details, so the screen can route in place. |
| `onInstall` | `() => void` | Called by Install now. |
| `onSkip?` | `() => void` | Called by Skip; omit when the update cannot be skipped now and the button is not drawn. |
| `pending?` | `'install' \| 'skip'` | The action in flight: its button shows a spinner and the other is disabled. |
| `error?` | `string` | Why the last action failed, set as text under the body; cleared by the screen on the next try. |

### ViewHeader

The header of a view pushed in place of another: back, title, an optional status at the right.

- **Use when:** a view replaces the popover body and the reader must be able to return, as the Limits strip does.
- **States:** default, crumb, back hover, back focus-visible
- **Source:** `src/blocks/ViewHeader.tsx`
- **Stories:** 4

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | The view's name, a heading. |
| `onBack?` | `() => void` | Goes back to the view this one replaced; shows the Back button, and focus lands on it on mount. |
| `status?` | `ReactNode` | What sits at the right: the strip passes "Applies now" with a green dot. |
| `crumb?` | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` | The view this one sits under, drawn as a link before the title: "Profiles ›". |
| `action?` | `ReactNode` | What sits at the right of the title, such as Remove. |

### VmRow

One virtual machine this host runs, as a row that opens in place like a gate: an icon for its status (serving, idle, booting, stopping, unmanaged; a dashed ring while the list is stale), its kind, what it serves (`3 jobs`, a job name; nothing otherwise, the icon says the rest) and its age. No slot number: it is the supervisor's index and means nothing to a reader. Pressing it lists its state in words when it is settling, stopping or unmanaged, what it was given (CPU, memory) and, for Linux, its free disk. With none of those known it does not open. The job name is GitHub's text, set as a text node on one line.

- **Use when:** the popover's Virtual machines section, one row per VM that is not stopped.
- **States:** serving Linux, serving macOS, idle, booting, stopping, unmanaged, open, no spec, long job name, dim
- **Source:** `src/blocks/VmRow.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vm` | `VmRowModel` | The VM: its kind, what it serves, its status and tone, what it was given and its age. |
| `dim?` | `boolean` | The last known list while the supervisor is unreachable: neutral by the model, the age `—`. |
| `open` | `boolean` | Whether its detail shows. One VM is open at a time; the screen keeps which. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called when the row is pressed. |

### VmSection

The label line and rows of the VMs this host runs. Each row opens in place to say what that VM was given. The screen decides whether to render it at all: with no VM there is no section, and an idle popover still shows it, since a running VM holds its memory.

- **Use when:** the popover, under this host's gauges and above Other hosts, whenever a VM is up.
- **States:** default, one row, a row open, stale, no sizes
- **Source:** `src/blocks/VmSection.tsx`
- **Stories:** 5

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `VmRowModel[]` | The VMs to show, Linux first and then macOS by slot, stopped ones left out. |
| `asOf` | `string \| null` | `as of 3m ago`, set while the list is stale, at the label's right. |
| `dim` | `boolean` | The list is stale (the supervisor is unreachable): its rows are neutral. |
| `openKey?` | `string \| null` | The key of the open row, if any. One VM is open at a time; the screen keeps which. |
| `onOpenChange?` | `(key: string \| null) => void` | Called with a row's key when it opens, `null` when it closes. |

## Screens

Each surface's screens, composed from the kit.

### Activity

Activity (A1): everything the daemon kept in memory, newest first, filtered by facet and search. It has no actions. The filters live in the query string so a view can be linked.

- **Use when:** the dashboard's `/activity` view, inside the Dashboard shell.
- **States:** busy, filtered, row open, run phases open, search with no match, empty, stale
- **Source:** `src/screens/Activity.tsx`
- **Stories:** 7

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stale?` | `boolean` | The last poll is old or failed: the header says "Stale". |
| `initialQuery?` | `string` | The filters as a query string (`?kind=fault`). Given, the view starts from it and leaves the address bar alone; omitted, it reads and writes `location.search` (ADR-0054 § 5). |
| `openFirstMessage?` | `boolean` | Opens the first row that carries a message at first, for a story. |
| `openFirstRun?` | `boolean` | Opens the first finished run at first, for a story. |
| `loadRun?` | `(runner: string) => Promise<RunFootprint \| null>` | Reads a finished run's phases when its row opens. The daemon's `/api/runs/:runner` when omitted; stories pass fixtures. |

### Dashboard

The dashboard: the sidebar (brand, host card, the views, an update card) and the view chosen in it. A pure function of the polled state; the entry polls, routes and runs actions.

- **Use when:** the dashboard entry at `/`, `/activity`, `/jobs`, `/memory` and `/maintenance`. Settings is its own page.
- **States:** connecting, overview, activity, jobs, memory, maintenance, stale, session ended, update pending, quiet
- **Source:** `src/screens/Dashboard.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `DaemonState \| null` | The last good snapshot, or null before the first poll answers. |
| `now` | `number` | Wall-clock ms the views format ages against. |
| `stale` | `boolean` | The last good poll is too old (screens.md S10). |
| `sessionEnded` | `string \| null` | Why the session ended (a 401), or null. |
| `run` | `(action: DashboardAction) => Promise<void>` | Runs an action, then polls. |
| `view` | `ViewId` | The view shown; the shell changes it as the sidebar is used. |
| `onNavigate` | `(view: ViewId) => void` | Called with the view the sidebar chose. The entry pushes its path. |
| `loadJobs?` | `JobsProps['load']` | Reads the Jobs view. The daemon's `/api/jobs` when omitted; stories pass fixtures. |
| `loadRun?` | `ActivityProps['loadRun']` | Reads one run's phases for Activity. The daemon's `/api/runs/:runner` when omitted; stories pass fixtures. |

### Jobs

Jobs (/jobs, ADR-0056 § 5): one row per job class over a window, saying where its runs' time went (each phase's median, the job split into setup, steps and post steps), whether they waited or ran (the parked share and the gate that bound most often), and whether they were starved or idle (CPU used against reserved, time lost to throttling, bytes moved). A class under the profiling threshold is shown as profiling and sorts last. Anything not measured says so; it is never drawn as zero.

- **Use when:** the dashboard's `/jobs` view, inside the Dashboard shell.
- **States:** busy, loading, empty, failed, profiling class, macOS class, stale
- **Source:** `src/screens/Jobs.tsx`
- **Stories:** 7

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stale?` | `boolean` | The last state poll is old or failed: the header says "Stale". |
| `load?` | `(days: number) => Promise<JobsView>` | Reads the view for a window, in days. The daemon's `/api/jobs` when omitted; stories pass fixtures. |
| `initialDays?` | `WindowDays` | The window the view starts on. Default 7 days. |

### LimitsView

The popover's Limits view (settings/anatomy.md § 5): the engine's memory as a bar, then one stepper per live autolimiter knob. Each press shows at once and sends one `set_config` for that knob after 400 ms without another press on it; each row keeps its own status.

- **Use when:** the popover body after an open gate's Adjust limits or Limits… is pressed. It replaces the whole card, the popover's header included, and brings its own back header.
- **States:** loaded, applying, applied, error, CPU warning, ceiling auto, ceiling off, unavailable, older daemon, loading
- **Source:** `src/screens/LimitsView.tsx`
- **Stories:** 10

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snap` | `Snapshot \| null` | The latest snapshot; `null` before the first one (the loading frame). |
| `invoke` | `Invoke` | Runs a Tauri command. |
| `onBack` | `() => void` | Back to the main view. |
| `onOpenSettings` | `() => void` | Opens All settings: the dashboard's /settings page, through the app. |
| `onReconnect?` | `() => Promise<unknown> \| void` | Re-reads the snapshot; the unavailable state's Reconnect. |
| `initialRows?` | `Rows` | Row states the view starts with (a story's open state). |

### Maintenance

The dashboard's Maintenance view (screens.md § 4, S13, S15): every action that changes what this host does. A row of control tiles (Host, Docker admission, Updates, Jobs), each its state with its action; Repository holds and Golden images side by side below; Drain behind a confirmation, last. A failure is the daemon's own text under the fact it belongs to.

- **Use when:** the dashboard's `/maintenance` view. A pure function of the state it is handed; actions go through `run`.
- **States:** running, paused, draining, held, repository holds, no golden image, golden failed, update ready, hold dialog open, drain confirm open, action failed
- **Source:** `src/screens/Maintenance.tsx`
- **Stories:** 11

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stale?` | `boolean` | The last good poll is older than the shell's staleness bound (S10): the live dot turns amber "Stale". |

### Memory

Memory (/memory, M1): the budget, then every job class with its caps and measured peaks, the limits behind admission and what parked jobs. A selected class opens beside the table, where its cap can be pinned (docs/design/dashboard/screens.md § 4).

- **Use when:** the dashboard's `/memory` view, inside the Dashboard shell. Its warnings are the Overview's `warning:` alarms, keyed by class: each carries Dismiss, and a dismissed one folds into "N dismissed" under them (ADR-0064).
- **States:** busy, class selected, pinned class selected, pin saving, pin failed, empty, stale, warning dismissable, warnings dismissed
- **Source:** `src/screens/Memory.tsx`
- **Stories:** 9

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stale?` | `boolean` | The last poll failed: the header says Stale and the numbers are the last good ones. |
| `initialQuery?` | `string` | The query string the view starts from, `?class=acme/web::1::build`; the page's own when omitted (stories pass one). |
| `initialFilter?` | `ClassFilter` | The filter the table starts on. |
| `initialPending?` | `boolean` | A pin save already in flight, as a story shows it. |
| `initialError?` | `string` | A failed pin save's text, as a story shows it. |
| `initialDismissedOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether the dismissed warnings show at first (a story's open state). |

### Overview

The dashboard's home view (screens.md § 4): is the host healthy, what is it doing, what needs me. The memory budget, four since-start tiles, the jobs in flight and the latest activity, and a rail with the alarms, the host and the learned caps. Host actions (Reconcile, Pause, Hold, Drain) live in Maintenance (S13); an alarm card keeps the one fix it names.

- **Use when:** the dashboard's `/` view. A pure function of the state it is handed; actions go through `run`.
- **States:** busy, healthy, fresh host (empty panels), stale, alarm action failed, alarms dismissed, dismissed open, trust changes acknowledged
- **Source:** `src/screens/Overview.tsx`
- **Stories:** 7

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stale?` | `boolean` | The last good poll is older than the shell's staleness bound (S10): the live dot turns amber "Stale". |
| `defaultDismissedOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether the dismissed alarms show when the view first renders (a story's open state). |

### Popover

The tray popover (popover.md, popover/anatomy.md): does faber need me? The header and its ⋯ menu, then every active issue, the gates (bars that open in place), the job groups with their pips, the virtual machines (rows that open in place), other hosts, and Pause or Resume. While job groups show it is 620 px in two columns, gauges and hosts left and the groups right, folded at the gauges' height into compact lines; otherwise a 308 px column. Offline it collapses to the dashboard link; before the first snapshot it shows the loading frame.

- **Use when:** the Tauri popover window, through `ui/popover/main.tsx`, which feeds it snapshots.
- **States:** loading, idle, idle with a VM up, idle with a stale peer, an issue and no jobs, running, waiting, finished, busy, busy overflow, folded into compact lines, folded past the compact lines, a folded group open, folded list open, attention list open, a gate open, a gate open while jobs wait, a gate open while idle, a VM open, paused and frozen, attention rows, dismissed rows, dismissed rows open, all dismissed, trust changes acknowledged, mirror down, mirror passing through, mirror image missing, macOS jobs held, action failed, two actions in flight, VMs stale, menu open, limits view, offline
- **Source:** `src/screens/Popover.tsx`
- **Stories:** 45

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snap` | `Snapshot \| null` | The latest snapshot from the app; `null` before the first one arrives (the loading frame). |
| `now` | `number` | The time the snapshot is read at, in ms: ages and lingering pips count from it. |
| `seen?` | `ReadonlyMap<number, Inflight>` | Live jobs this app has seen, by id, so a finished run joins its own group. |
| `invoke` | `Invoke` | Runs a Tauri command. |
| `menuOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether the ⋯ menu is open; the app closes it when the window loses focus. |
| `onMenuOpenChange?` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called when the ⋯ menu opens or closes. |
| `defaultOpenGroup?` | `string \| null` | The group open when the screen first renders (a story's open state). |
| `defaultOpenGate?` | `GaugeKey \| null` | The gate open when the screen first renders (a story's open state). |
| `defaultOpenVm?` | `string \| null` | The VM row open when the screen first renders (a story's open state), by its key (`linux-0`). |
| `onSnapshot?` | `(snap: Snapshot) => void` | Called with the snapshot the app holds when the Limits view's Reconnect re-reads it. |
| `defaultView?` | `'main' \| 'limits'` | The view shown when the screen first renders (a story's open state). |
| `defaultJobsOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether the folded job groups show when the screen first renders (a story's open state). |
| `defaultAttentionOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether the folded attention rows show when the screen first renders (a story's open state). |
| `defaultDismissedOpen?` | `boolean` | Whether the dismissed rows show when the screen first renders (a story's open state). |
| `maxHeight?` | `number` | The tallest the card may grow, even to hold an open group: the window's cap by default. |

### PopoverFallback

What the popover shows when a snapshot it cannot draw arrives: the header, one line saying so, and the two ways out, the panel and Quit. The next snapshot tries the screen again.

- **Use when:** only as the popover entry's error fallback (`PopoverApp`).
- **States:** default
- **Source:** `src/screens/Popover.tsx`
- **Stories:** 45

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invoke` | `Invoke` | Runs a Tauri command. |

### Settings

The Settings page (anatomy.md § 5, Settings): the nav, the selected section rendered from the schema, the raw `config.toml` editor, and the save bar. One draft at a time between form and text.

- **Use when:** the dashboard's /settings page. Its state is seeded by `initial` for stories and tests.
- **States:** loading, loaded, saving, saved with restart pending, invalid, refused, stale, can't load, started with flags, no profiles, raw clean, raw changed, raw TOML error, raw refused, raw blocked by form changes, raw stale, session ended
- **Source:** `src/screens/Settings.tsx`
- **Stories:** 56

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api?` | `SettingsApi` | The daemon calls; the page passes `settings/api`, stories and tests pass fakes. |
| `initial?` | `Partial<SettingsState>` | Seeds the state. With a `view` the page does not load first. |
